answer: Each agent identity must lock collateral plus pay a non-refundable fee in a scarce external asset before it can submit work or vote. A thousand fake agents therefore need a thousand deposits live at once. Collusion or failed spot-checks slash the stake, so the attacker must finance the entire identity set in real value and lose it when caught; forgery costs more than it earns. Per-epoch prompts, such as modelling ocean sampling or delta hedging of a quartz-grade vault, keep accounts costly to mass-produce.
